text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Attorney-General Amos Wako says the government is liaising with Canadian authorities to have runaway banker Alnoor Kassam extradited to face 16 criminal charges over the 1993 collapse of Trade Bank.

- Parliament passes a motion which, for the first time in independent Kenya, will give bright secondary school students from disadvantaged areas and vulnerable groups a second chance to qualify for university admission, if they fail to attain university admission cut-off points.
- Some 800 primary school pupils in Nyambene and Tharaka-Nithi districts (of eastern province) desert school following land clashes along the districts' borders.
- Police net more than 3,000 people suspected of being involved in criminal activities in one of the biggest operations ever in the Kenyan capital of Nairobi.

- Deposit Protection Fund Board, appointed liquidator of the collapsed Kenya Finance Bank by the Central Bank of Kenya, issues statement saying small depositors start receiving payments for their protected deposits on January 6, 1997.
- Kenya Tea Development Authority announces tea growers will be paid nearly 5.4 billion shillings beginning next week.
- As a result of an intensified academic programme adopted by Kenyatta University, students at the university can now graduate after three years of study instead of the mandatory four.
